subject: Biology
description: Human heart and circulation — chambers, valves, double circulation, cardiac cycle, blood pressure, ECG, common diseases.

questions.stem: The HUMAN HEART has HOW MANY CHAMBERS?
questions.explanation: HUMAN HEART — 4 CHAMBERS: 2 ATRIA (upper, receive blood) + 2 VENTRICLES (lower, pump blood out). RIGHT side (pulmonary circuit): RIGHT ATRIUM receives DEOXYGENATED blood from body (via vena cava) → RIGHT VENTRICLE → pulmonary ARTERY → LUNGS (oxygenation). LEFT side (systemic circuit): LEFT ATRIUM receives OXYGENATED blood from lungs (via pulmonary VEINS) → LEFT VENTRICLE → AORTA → BODY. SEPTUM separates left and right (no direct blood mixing in healthy heart). HEART-CHAMBER COUNT in animals: (1) MAMMALS, BIRDS — 4 chambers (efficient double circulation). (2) REPTILES — 3 chambers (incomplete septum in ventricle; crocodile has 4). (3) AMPHIBIANS — 3 chambers (2 atria, 1 ventricle). (4) FISH — 2 chambers (1 atrium, 1 ventricle). KEY HEART STATS: (1) WEIGHT ~300 g. (2) Beats ~60-100/min at rest, up to ~200/min during exercise. (3) Pumps ~5 L blood/min at rest. (4) ~2 BILLION beats in average lifetime. (5) Heart muscle = MYOCARDIUM (involuntary, striated cardiac muscle); doesn't fatigue normally. CARDIAC OUTPUT = stroke volume × heart rate. UPSC angle: heart anatomy in NCERT Class 11; biology PT and prelims often have one heart-related Q. PYQ FREQUENCY: 4-chamber heart in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which artery carries DEOXYGENATED blood (an exception to general rule)?
questions.explanation: EXCEPTION TO GENERAL RULE: 'arteries carry oxygenated blood; veins carry deoxygenated blood' has TWO EXCEPTIONS — (1) PULMONARY ARTERY carries DEOXYGENATED blood from RIGHT VENTRICLE to LUNGS. (2) PULMONARY VEINS carry OXYGENATED blood from LUNGS back to LEFT ATRIUM. BLOOD VESSEL TYPES: (a) ARTERIES — thick, muscular walls; carry blood AWAY from heart; high pressure. (b) VEINS — thinner walls, valves to prevent backflow; carry blood TO heart; low pressure. (c) CAPILLARIES — single-cell-thick walls; site of GAS/NUTRIENT EXCHANGE between blood and tissues. KEY ARTERIES (memorize): (1) AORTA — largest artery; carries oxygenated blood from left ventricle. (2) CAROTID ARTERIES — neck; supply brain. (3) RENAL ARTERIES — kidneys. (4) HEPATIC ARTERY — liver (oxygenated). (5) FEMORAL ARTERY — thigh; pulse check site. (6) RADIAL ARTERY — wrist; pulse check site. (7) CORONARY ARTERIES — supply heart muscle itself. CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE (CAD) — blockage of coronary arteries = heart attack ('myocardial infarction'). India has high CAD rates due to genetics + lifestyle. UPSC angle: NCD (Non-Communicable Diseases) burden — heart disease, diabetes, cancer increasing in India. PYQ FREQUENCY: pulmonary-artery exception in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: NORMAL BLOOD PRESSURE in adults is approximately:
questions.explanation: NORMAL BP: ~120/80 mmHg (systolic/diastolic). SYSTOLIC = pressure when heart CONTRACTS (peak); DIASTOLIC = pressure when heart RELAXES (minimum). UNITS: mmHg (millimetres of mercury) — measured by sphygmomanometer (cuff-based). BP CATEGORIES (per modern AHA/ACC 2017): (1) NORMAL: <120/<80. (2) ELEVATED: 120-129/<80. (3) STAGE 1 HYPERTENSION: 130-139 / 80-89. (4) STAGE 2 HYPERTENSION: ≥140 / ≥90. (5) HYPERTENSIVE CRISIS: >180 / >120 (medical emergency). HYPOTENSION: <90/60 (low BP, dizziness). HYPERTENSION ('SILENT KILLER') — risk for: heart attack, stroke, kidney disease, vision loss, aneurysms. INDIA — ~30% adults have hypertension (~25 crore people). KEY CAUSES: high salt intake (Indians average 11 g/day vs WHO 5 g recommendation), obesity, sedentary lifestyle, stress, smoking, alcohol, genetics. TREATMENT: lifestyle + drugs (ACE inhibitors, ARBs, beta-blockers, diuretics, calcium-channel blockers). UPSC angle: NATIONAL PROGRAMME for PREVENTION & CONTROL of NCDs (NPCDCS) — addresses hypertension, diabetes, cancer, stroke. WHITE-COAT SYNDROME: BP elevated only at clinic — recommend home BP monitoring. PYQ FREQUENCY: normal BP in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: The pacemaker of the human heart, generating the heartbeat rhythm, is the:
questions.explanation: SA NODE (Sino-Atrial node) — natural PACEMAKER of the heart; located in the WALL OF RIGHT ATRIUM near where superior vena cava enters. Generates electrical impulses ~70-80 times/min at rest (autonomous self-excitatory cells). HEART CONDUCTION SYSTEM (in order of signal propagation): (1) SA NODE generates impulse. (2) Spreads through ATRIA → both atria contract simultaneously. (3) AV NODE (Atrio-Ventricular) — receives signal; brief delay (~0.1 sec) — ensures atria empty BEFORE ventricles contract. (4) BUNDLE OF HIS — transmits signal to ventricles via septum. (5) LEFT and RIGHT BUNDLE BRANCHES. (6) PURKINJE FIBRES — spread signal through ventricle walls; ventricles contract. ECG (ELECTROCARDIOGRAM): records this electrical activity. KEY WAVES: (a) P WAVE — atrial depolarization (atrial contraction). (b) QRS COMPLEX — ventricular depolarization (most prominent). (c) T WAVE — ventricular repolarization. ARTIFICIAL PACEMAKER: implanted device replaces malfunctioning SA node — ~600,000 implanted globally per year; battery life 5-10 years. CONDITIONS treated: bradycardia (slow heart rate), AV block, arrhythmias. INDIAN BIOMEDICAL: Trichi-based AIIMS-Delhi successfully implanted India's first 'leadless' pacemaker (2018). UPSC GS-3 health-tech angle. PYQ FREQUENCY: SA node 'pacemaker' in NEET, NCERT Class 11, AIIMS PG entrance.

questions.stem: DOUBLE CIRCULATION in mammals means blood passes through the heart:
questions.explanation: DOUBLE CIRCULATION — blood passes through the heart TWICE in each complete cycle (mammals + birds): (1) PULMONARY CIRCULATION: deoxygenated blood from BODY → right atrium → right ventricle → PULMONARY ARTERY → LUNGS (oxygenation) → PULMONARY VEINS → left atrium. (2) SYSTEMIC CIRCULATION: oxygenated blood from left atrium → left ventricle → AORTA → all body tissues (delivers O₂, takes CO₂) → vena cava → right atrium. ADVANTAGE: Oxygenated and deoxygenated blood are NEVER MIXED. Allows HIGH-PRESSURE delivery to body (left ventricle wall is THICK, generates high BP). Enables ENDOTHERMY (warm-blooded metabolism). CONTRAST WITH FISH (single circulation): blood passes through heart ONCE per cycle: heart → gills → body → heart. Lower efficiency, lower pressure body delivery — but suits cold-blooded fish lifestyle. AMPHIBIANS, REPTILES (most): incomplete double circulation — some mixing of oxygenated/deoxygenated blood in heart. CROCODILES — uniquely have 4-chambered heart (like mammals) but with FORAMEN of PANIZZA (small connection) — can divert blood for diving. WHO discovered: WILLIAM HARVEY (1628, England) — published 'De Motu Cordis' establishing the concept of CIRCULATION; revolutionary in medical history. Before Harvey, GALEN's (Roman) view of blood being CONSUMED by tissues persisted for 1500 years. PYQ FREQUENCY: double circulation in NEET, NCERT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which valve prevents BACKFLOW of blood from LEFT VENTRICLE to LEFT ATRIUM?
questions.explanation: MITRAL VALVE (also called BICUSPID, has 2 flaps) — between LEFT ATRIUM and LEFT VENTRICLE; prevents backflow during ventricular contraction. NAMED 'mitral' for resemblance to a bishop's mitre (hat). 4 HEART VALVES (memorize): (1) TRICUSPID (3 flaps) — right atrium ↔ right ventricle. (2) PULMONARY (semilunar) — right ventricle ↔ pulmonary artery. (3) MITRAL/BICUSPID (2 flaps) — left atrium ↔ left ventricle. (4) AORTIC (semilunar) — left ventricle ↔ aorta. FUNCTION: ensure ONE-WAY blood flow; prevent backflow. SOUNDS: 'LUB-DUB' heartbeat = (1) 'LUB' — closing of AV valves (mitral + tricuspid) at start of ventricular systole. (2) 'DUB' — closing of semilunar valves (aortic + pulmonary) at end of ventricular systole. ABNORMAL: (1) MITRAL STENOSIS — narrowed valve, often from rheumatic fever. (2) MITRAL REGURGITATION — leaky valve. (3) MURMURS — abnormal sounds from valve disease. (4) Mitral PROLAPSE — valve flops. TREATMENT: VALVE REPLACEMENT — mechanical (lasts forever, needs blood thinners) or biological (porcine, bovine — lasts ~10-20 years). INDIA: ~1 lakh valve surgeries/year; AIIMS, Apollo, Fortis are top centers. UPSC HEALTH PILLARS: PMJAY (Ayushman Bharat) covers cardiac surgeries up to ₹5 lakh. PYQ FREQUENCY: heart valves in NEET, AIIMS, NCERT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: RBCs (red blood cells) in MAMMALS are:
questions.explanation: MAMMALIAN RBCs (ERYTHROCYTES): (1) ANUCLEATE — LOSE NUCLEUS during maturation (unique to mammals; other vertebrates retain nucleus). (2) BICONCAVE DISC shape — increases surface area for gas exchange + flexibility to squeeze through capillaries. (3) Filled with HEMOGLOBIN (Hb) — iron-containing protein, binds O₂ and CO₂. (4) ~5 million per microlitre of blood. (5) Lifespan ~120 DAYS; replaced continuously by BONE MARROW. (6) Removed by SPLEEN (the 'graveyard' of RBCs). RBC FUNCTIONS: (1) O₂ transport — Hb binds O₂ in lungs (~98% saturation), releases in tissues. (2) CO₂ transport — partially as carbamino-Hb; mostly as bicarbonate. (3) Maintain blood pH via buffering. WHY ANUCLEATE: maximizes Hb capacity (no nucleus = more cytoplasmic room for Hb); but reduces RBC lifespan (no DNA repair). HEMOGLOBIN: 4 protein chains (2α, 2β) + 4 heme groups (each containing Fe²⁺); each Hb binds 4 O₂. ANEMIA: low Hb (< 12 g/dL women, < 13 men). INDIA — major issue: ~52% women anaemic (NFHS-5, 2019-21). Causes: iron deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, sickle cell, thalassemia. SICKLE CELL ANEMIA: hereditary, common in tribal India + Africa; sickle-shaped RBCs cause blood-clots, anaemia. WORLD SICKLE CELL DAY: 19 June. PYQ FREQUENCY: RBC structure in NEET, AIIMS, NCERT 1× per cycle.
